messages:
jon: Heads-up — noticed anomalies in authz logs after last night's KMS rewrap. Some embeddings API calls returned 200 for chat routes briefly.
li: Wait what. Can you paste the log lines?
jon: sure, here's the edge log snippet 
```
2026-03-12T03:22:14Z INFO route=embeddings request_id=abc123 auth_scope=embeddings model=gpt-embed-3 result=OK forwarded_route=/v1/chat/completions allowed=true key_tag=rewrap-2026-03-12
2026-03-12T03:22:15Z WARN route=chat request_id=abc124 auth_scope=embeddings model=gpt-chat-3 result=access_granted_via_fallback key_tag=rewrap-2026-03-12
```
marta: oof. So token had embeddings scope but chat accepted it? That sounds like scope enforcement used KMS tag mismatch as truth.
li: I see key_tag rewrap metadata used by authz service to map scopes for new wrapped keys; if tag lookup returns empty during rewrap window we fall back to legacy allowlist mapping. Maybe fallback allowed embeddings->chat for legacy tokens.
andrew: Can we confirm this is a short timing window correlated to rewrap? Check KMS event timeline.
sec-bot: KMS rewrap completed 2026-03-12T03:22:10Z for key kc-42. Rotation job reported success across regions at 03:22:09Z.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy of authz-config v2.7 started 03:21:50Z, finished 03:22:05Z.
jon: Correlation looks strong. Rewrap completed while authz canary was still converging. A read of key-tag cache returned stale value for ~6s. During that time, scope enforcement used a permissive fallback.
marta: How many requests affected? Estimate?
li: Quick query: ~1.6k requests over the 12s window across staging and prod edges. Most were retries; ~210 unique tokens.
andrew: Severity? Any signs of data exfil or drift?
jon: No user-visible data exfil found. Chat endpoints returned allowed responses but logs show no high-sensitivity payloads. Impact = low->medium, but definitely an authz violation.
li: Immediate mitigation: 1) Force key-tag cache flush and disable permissive fallback. 2) Backfill audit logs with key-tag mapping at time-of-request. 3) Add short-term rule: fail-open -> fail-closed toggle for rewrap windows.
marta: I pushed a config change to authz to disable permissive fallback (canary) — will roll to prod now. @deploy-bot please run a fast rollback if needed.
deploy-bot: Canary updated, config rollout started 03:25:01Z.
sec-bot: Noted: created incident INC-2026-0312-KMS-1. Assigned to eng-security and eng-runtime.
li: Action items for postmortem: - add end-to-end test covering KMS rewrap timing + authz cache eviction - instrument metric for fallback usage count - require key-tag read before allowing scope mapping during rotation windows - add audit backfill automation
andrew: Also add a chaos test: simulate KMS metadata lag while deploying authz config canaries.
jon: For now I ran a script to re-evaluate all requests with affected tokens and re-check scope mapping; flagged ~210 requests for audit review.
marta: Good. Please include sample curl we used for repro in the ticket: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xyz" -H "X-Key-Tag: rewrap-2026-03-12" https://edge.internal/v1/chat/completions
```
li: Follow-up policy question: should key rewrap be atomic across service planes? Maybe require pause on authz canaries during KMS rotations.
andrew: That is heavy. Alternative: authz must gracefully handle tag-missing by rejecting, never by falling back.
jon: Agree — fail closed is preferred here. We'll change fallback to explicit opt-in for legacy migration flows.
marta: I'll own the postmortem. Tentative timeline: publish within 72h. Li and Andrew to own remediation PRs. Jon to assist with audit backfill script.
sec-bot: Audit log entry created for every re-evaluated request.
li: Also propose to add a short TTL on key-tag cache to reduce window. Current TTL is 60s; lower to 5s for rotation-sensitive tags. Need perf check.
andrew: Perf risk but worth it for security-critical tags. Run perf tests in staging.
jon: Quick note: no users reported incidents yet, so public impact = none. We'll still notify customers if we find any cross-model misuse.
marta: Thanks everyone. Will coordinate postmortem and link to INC-2026-0312-KMS-1.
li: I'll open the remediation PRs today and add tests.
andrew: I'll schedule the chaos test for next week.
jon: Leaving more debug traces in logs for the next 24h.
sec-bot: Incident severity set to Sev3.
marta: ending thread — follow-ups tracked in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
